answer: Persistent Trail Quota. Each identity gets a finite action budget tied to a slow clock, spent by writing to a shared append-only log. The log remembers every agent's path through a canyon of epochs; a clone reusing another's history collides at the same checkpoints and gets frozen. New identities must wander a warm-up period collecting quill-signed timestamps from unrelated peers before full budget unlocks. An attacker pays that full warm-up cost, plus lost budget on each burned clone, making duplication linearly expensive.
